summary:

Other executives including Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella also endorsed the idea of embedding independent evaluators in companies.

title: ‘I spend a bagful of money and don’t fill a bag’: the energy crisis hits Bangladesh
summary:
The country has been left in the dark as it endures power cuts caused by the Iran war and reliance on gas imports

At 1am, Halder’s alarm goes off and the 34-year-old Bangladeshi bank employee rises and heads to her kitchen. She is up at this time not for work but to cook for her family. An energy crisis paralysing the capital, Dhaka, a city of almost 40 million people, means this has become the only time when the piped gas supply is strong enough to allow cooking.

The city now operates in darkness, as people try to continue their lives with power even in public areas shut off early in the evening to preserve energy.

title: To protect democracy, Democrats should talk about corruption – not authoritarianism | Jared Abbott and Joan C Williams
summary:
The party needs to thread the needle between college-educated and working-class voters. Our survey offers a way

Resisting authoritarianism is the second-highest priority for Democrats’ college-educated base. But for working-class Americans, it’s only the 19th priority (out of 20), we found in a new survey. The gap between these two groups was larger than on any other issues: elites prioritized resisting authoritarianism an astonishing 33 percentage points more than non-elites did.

Democrats’ dilemma is that their college-educated base insists they stand up to Donald Trump’s attacks on democracy, but they also need to win working-class votes. The way to thread that needle is to recognize that what’s needed to defend democracy in the short term is different from what’s needed to defend it in the long term.
